newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: New home search powers for Ivorian security forces.
newsitem.headline: New home search powers for Ivorian security forces.

text.p: Ivory Coast's parliament voted a new law on Monday giving police and security forces greater powers to raid and search private homes at any hour of the day or night.

Parliament, where President Henri Konan Bedie's Democratic Party (PDCI) enjoys a crushing majority, approved the new law by 115 votes to 13 but added a clause insisting on advance judicial or administrative authorisation.

Bedie, anxious to curb a rash of armed robberies and present the West African nation as safe for foreign investors and Ivorians alike, lobbied hard for security forces to be allowed to raid homes on their own authority.
Human rights groups and many ordinary Ivorians expressed misgivings about the idea, arguing criminals could gain entry to homes of unsuspecting householders disguised as police.
Previously, between 9 p.m. and 4 a.m., security forces could only raid private homes on the orders of a judge.

The crime wave has hit all sections of the community in Ivory Coast's towns and cities. Rich and poor areas, Ivorians and foreigners have been victims of armed criminals. In August, an estimated 10 cars a day were stolen at gunpoint in Abidjan.

The government has stepped up patrols by armed paramilitary gendarmes in parts of Abidjan, the commercial capital. Last year, parliament voted a new law authorising the death penalty for robbery with violence in certain cases as well as murder.
The death penalty, although on the statute book, has not been applied since independence from France.
